title: Cascade traffic quarantine and safe failover play for mixed-hosted/dedicated tenants
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: This ticket defines an operational play and emergency patch plan to (1) quickly quarantine cascading unhealthy traffic across regions, (2) execute safe tenant-aware failovers for mixed hosted+dedi deployments, and (3) apply a targeted bugfix to prevent KV-cache desync during large-scale resharding. Motivation: Recent customer escalations indicated a pattern where a partial networking degradation in a single region caused amplified request retries and leader re-election churn that spilled traffic into healthy regions. For hosted tenants and dedicated pools this produced noisy neighbor effects and KV cache staleness that required manual tenant rehomes in multiple cases. Goal: Create a reproducible runbook, a small hotfix, and automated traffic quarantine gates that reduce blast radius and give SREs an actionable, low-risk path to restore customer-serving capacity without full region switchover.
comments: 2026-03-05 - Aisha Patel: Initial write-up after sync with SRE and Support. Summarized observed failure modes from Customer Support tickets #CS-8873 and #CS-8891. Noted KV cache rehydration failures and leader lease flapping during tenant rehome events.

During spikes routing started oversubscribing a small set of warm nodes. Proposed quarantine gate: detect >3x deviation in request completion latency + 40% increase in retry rate per tenant in 30s window, then mark tenant traffic as 'quarantine' and route to low-latency fallback model variant or dedicated warm standby.

acceptance_criteria: 1) Runbook written and reviewed by SRE/Support/Product/Legal. 2) Hotfix PR merged and smoke-tested in staging. 3) Quarantine gate feature flag is deployable and exercised in a canary region with documented metrics (kv_cache_miss_rate, retry_rate, tenant_p95). 4) CLI manual override documented and tested. 5) At least one cross-team rehearsal completed with playbook follow-through and customer comms practiced.
runbook: Overview: When a region shows signs of cascading failure (latency spike + retry amplification + KV cache degradation), the SRE on-call should: Step 0 - Triage: verify alerts on Grafana + check incident channel #incidents-cross-region. Step 1 - Identify scope: run 'redwood-admin observe tenants --region <REG> --since 30m' and look for tenants with retry_rate>3x and kv_cache_miss_rate>15%. Step 2 - Quarantine: execute 'redwood-admin traffic quarantine --tenant <TID> --policy safe-fallback' to mark traffic and route to warm standby or cheaper model variant. Quarantine is tenant-scoped, non-destructive, and reversible. Step 3 - KV Validation: after quarantine, run 'redwood-admin kv validate --tenant <TID>' and ensure committed_snapshot matches leader_snapshot. If mismatch, trigger 'kv reconcile' flow (requires approval from SRE lead). Step 4 - Controlled rehome (if necessary): if quarantine fails to restore, run tenant rehome with phased weight shift: 10% -> 33% -> 66% -> 100% over 10-minute windows, verifying p95 and error rates at each step. Step 5 - Post-action telemetry: annotate incident, collect metrics for 1h post-recovery, and initiate customer comms using approved templates. Emergency rollback: 'redwood-admin traffic unquarantine --tenant <TID>' or 'redwood-admin featureflag toggle traffic-quarantine false' (with audit).
postmortem_actions: - Complete ENG-990002 to fix sticky-routing metadata transfer during rehome. - Implement tenant-visible 'rehydration status' in Console (ENG-990003). - Add automatic snapshot verification hook in runtime leader election code (follow-up in runtime roadmap). - Add cost-estimation telemetry for quarantine fallback to measure customer bill impact. - Schedule quarterly DR drills covering hosted + dedicated mixed-scenarios.

Slack channel: #incidents-cross-region. Important: This play is intended to reduce customer-visible failures by avoiding full region cutovers; however, it will increase cross-region egress and temporary compute usage for warm standbys. Coordinate with Finance for cost-exposure estimates before wide rollout.
